paper_title: Reinforcement Learning Meets Large Language Models: A Survey of Advancements and Applications Across the LLM Lifecycle
paper_topic: Reinforcement Learning (RL) application in Large Language Models (LLMs), focusing on the full lifecycle from pre-training to alignment and reasoning (RLVR).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the rise of LLMs and the necessity of RL for alignment and reasoning. It highlights the shift from standard RLHF to Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) exemplified by models like DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI-o1. It outlines the survey's goal to cover the full RL lifecycle.

subsections.title: Related Surveys
subsections.description: Reviews existing surveys, noting their limitations such as narrow focus on alignment or lack of lifecycle coverage. It positions this survey as a comprehensive review covering pre-training, alignment, and the latest inference-time reasoning advancements.

subsections.title: Contribution Summary
subsections.description: Summarizes the paper's three main contributions: a lifecycle-based organization of RL methods, a focus on advanced RLVR technology, and a consolidation of resources including datasets, benchmarks, and frameworks.

sections.title: Preliminaries of Reinforcement Learning
sections.description: Establishes the theoretical foundations of RL, modeling the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). It distinguishes between the two primary paradigms used in LLM training: policy-based learning and value-based learning.

subsections.title: Policy Learning
subsections.description: Details methods that directly optimize the policy, including REINFORCE, Actor-Critic, TRPO, and PPO. It specifically highlights Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a key algorithm for reasoning models that eliminates the value network to save resources.

subsections.title: Value Learning
subsections.description: Explains methods that estimate value functions to derive policies, such as Q-learning, SARSA, and DQN. It notes that while less common in direct LLM generation due to action space size, these concepts influence specific techniques like exemplar selection.

sections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Pre-training Phase and Alignment Phase
sections.description: Reviews the application of RL in the early stages of the LLM lifecycle. It covers attempts to integrate RL into pre-training and details the established methods used for aligning models with human preferences.

subsections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Pre-training Phase
subsections.description: Discusses niche approaches to introducing RL during pre-training, such as reconstructing next-token prediction as a reasoning task, visual pre-training with RL, and 'mid-training' strategies to prepare models for RL scaling.

subsections.title: Classic Algorithms in the Alignment Phase
subsections.description: Summarizes standard alignment techniques including RLHF, Constitutional AI, RLAIF, and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). It touches on methods for mitigating reward hacking and optimizing for human utility.

subsections.title: Emerging Methods for Reward Model Design
subsections.description: Focuses on innovations in reward modeling, such as Reward Reasoning Models (RRM) that use Chain-of-Thought, generative process reward models, and rule-based rewards to improve the accuracy and generalization of feedback signals.

sections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Reasoning Phase
sections.description: The core section of the survey, focusing on RL with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). It explores how RL is used to enhance complex reasoning in math, code, and multimodal tasks, analyzing algorithms, experimental findings, and adaptive strategies.

subsections.title: Experimental Findings of RLVR in Improving the Reasoning Ability of LLMs
subsections.description: Analyzes whether RLVR truly creates new reasoning capabilities or merely acts as an efficient sampler. It discusses the 'entropy collapse' phenomenon, the necessity of explicit thinking processes, and the boundaries of model capability.

subsections.title: Recent Advances in RL Algorithms for LLMs
subsections.description: Chronicles the latest algorithms post-2024, including improvements to GRPO, DAPO for long sequences, Open-Reasoner-Zero, and various hybrid strategies combining SFT and RL to stabilize training and improve efficiency.

subsections.title: Application of RLVR in Multimodal Reasoning
subsections.description: Examines the application of RLVR to Vision-Language Models (VLMs), video reasoning, and embodied intelligence. It covers specific models like Vision-R1 and techniques for visual generation and spatial reasoning.

subsections.title: Adaptive Reasoning
subsections.description: Discusses methods to control the length and depth of Chain-of-Thought reasoning. It covers 'budget forcing', thinking mode switching (long vs. short), and difficulty-aware resource allocation during inference.

subsections.title: RLVR for Agent
subsections.description: Addresses the challenges of applying RL to multi-turn agents, such as delayed rewards and long horizons. It reviews frameworks for tool use, memory management, and environment interaction (e.g., Minecraft, web search).

subsections.title: Reinforcement Learning from Internal Feedback
subsections.description: Explores unsupervised or self-supervised RL methods that rely on internal signals like self-certainty or consistency rather than external labels, aiming to activate pre-trained knowledge without human supervision.

sections.title: Datasets and Benchmarks
sections.description: Surveys the data resources required for RL training and evaluation. It categorizes resources into synthetic data generation pipelines and established benchmarks for various domains.

subsections.title: Synthetic Data Generation
subsections.description: Describes frameworks for generating training data without human annotation, including methods for creating reasoning chains, tool-use trajectories, and difficulty-adapted questions to support RLVR.

subsections.title: Datasets and Benchmarks
subsections.description: Lists and categorizes standard benchmarks for alignment (e.g., HHH, HH-RLHF), code (APPS, SWE-bench), math (GSM8K, MATH), and general knowledge, used to evaluate RL-enhanced models.

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows the chronological lifecycle of an LLM. It begins with theoretical foundations, moves to Pre-training (early stage), then Alignment (standard post-training), and culminates in Reasoning (the current frontier/late-stage post-training). It concludes with the necessary supporting resources (Data/Benchmarks).
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The transition is evolutionary. Section 3 covers the 'classic' RLHF era (Alignment), while Section 4 transitions to the 'modern' RLVR era (Reasoning), reflecting the industry's shift from making models 'safe' to making them 'smart'.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The structure is heavily weighted towards Section 4 (Reasoning), which contains 6 subsections. This reflects the survey's focus on the most recent advancements (2024-2025) like DeepSeek-R1 and o1. Sections 2 and 3 provide necessary context but are less granular than the reasoning section.
key_strengths: Clear separation of 'Alignment' and 'Reasoning' phases, which clarifies the evolving role of RL.
Inclusion of a specific subsection on 'Experimental Findings' (4.1) which discusses the *nature* of intelligence emergence, not just algorithms.
Comprehensive taxonomy (referenced in text) that maps algorithms to specific lifecycle stages.
Timeliness: Dedicated focus on RLVR and GRPO, which are the immediate state-of-the-art techniques.
